lines.cap: To join the world's most famous secret society, a grown man drops one trouser leg, gets blindfolded, and is led around on a rope.
lines.say: To join the world's most famous secret society, a grown man drops one trouser leg, gets blindfolded, and is led around on a rope.

lines.cap: That's a Freemason initiation. One trouser leg up, one slipper on, and a rope around the neck called a cable tow.
lines.say: That's a Freemason initiation. One trouser leg up, one slipper on, and a rope around the neck called a cable tow.

lines.cap: It began with British stonemasons. The first Grand Lodge opened in London in 1717.
lines.say: It began with British stonemasons. The first Grand Lodge opened in London in 1717.

lines.cap: Around fourteen US presidents were Freemasons. George Washington laid the Capitol's first stone in a Masonic apron.
lines.say: Around fourteen US presidents were Freemasons. George Washington laid the Capitol's first stone in a Masonic apron.

lines.cap: Secret oaths. Secret handshakes. Temples full of symbols. The square, the compass, the all-seeing eye.
lines.say: Secret oaths. Secret handshakes. Temples full of symbols. The square, the compass, the all-seeing eye.

lines.cap: In 1826, a New Yorker threatened to publish their secrets. Then he vanished. America even got an Anti-Masonic political party.
lines.say: In 1826, a New Yorker threatened to publish their secrets. Then he vanished. America even got an Anti-Masonic political party.

lines.cap: Members today say it's mostly charity and dinners. Which is exactly what a secret society would say.
lines.say: Members today say it's mostly charity and dinners. Which is exactly what a secret society would say.
